description: Four polyphonic amplifiers with adjustable response curves, chained so that an unpatched output is added to the next channel and the four work as a mixer

params.text: Sets that channel's gain outright when nothing is patched to its CV jack, and scales that CV when something is; with a cable there, the slider at the top and 5V give unity gain
Sets that channel's response curve, from exponential at the far counter-clockwise end to linear at the far clockwise one
Adds a positive offset of up to 5V to that channel's control voltage before the curve is applied; with nothing patched to that channel's CV jack it is added straight to the gain instead

inputs.text: The signal that channel amplifies; the largest channel count among the four signal inputs sets the module's polyphony
Sets that channel's gain, scaled by the slider, offset by the knob and then bent by the response curve; 5V with the slider at the top gives unity gain

outputs.text: That channel's amplified signal, summed with any channel before it whose own output has no cable

notes: the outputs are normalled into one another: a channel whose output has no cable is added to the next channel's output, which is what makes the four a mixer.
a sum that passes ±10V is put through a saturator rather than clipped.
the lamp above a channel reports the polarity and size of that channel's mix, with one pair of colours for a monophonic signal and another for a polyphonic one.
with nothing patched to a channel's CV jack, that channel's offset knob is added straight to the slider, so gain can reach six times; the manual says the offset reaches the modulation alone.

inputs.4:

a negative voltage does nothing here; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 8V.
